---
title: "Research"
description: "Research themes in disordered and high-entropy oxides."
---

## High-entropy and entropy-stabilized oxides

How does configurational complexity alter the thermodynamics, structure and properties of an oxide? We study when entropy genuinely stabilizes a phase, how competing structures emerge, and how synthesis conditions determine the resulting material.

## Short-range order and local distortions

Average crystallographic symmetry can conceal chemically specific correlations and local structural distortions. We connect local order to composition, bonding and collective properties using complementary experimental and computational approaches.

## Predictive modelling of disordered materials

We use density-functional theory, cluster expansions and machine-learning interatomic potentials to explore configurational spaces that cannot be represented by a single conventional unit cell.

## Functional complex oxides

We investigate how chemical disorder can be used to tune optical, dielectric, piezoelectric and thermal behavior, with an emphasis on lead-free and resource-conscious materials.

## Methods

- Solid-state, solution and flux synthesis
- Laboratory and synchrotron X-ray diffraction
- Local-structure and thermal characterization
- Density-functional theory and lattice dynamics
- Cluster expansions and configurational sampling
- Machine-learning interatomic potentials
